nodes.title: Rooftop terrace site
nodes.summary: Terrace on a 9-storey building. No crane access and no room for a gantry: the reason drones were chosen.

nodes.title: Printed shell, 2.4 m
nodes.summary: Thin-walled, non-structural shell printed in place, layer by layer. Enclosure only.

nodes.title: Digital twin v4
nodes.summary: Design model, sliced into horizontal layers, with a stability check for every interim stage.

nodes.title: BuilDrone 1
nodes.summary: Quadrotor with cartridge extruder and delta arm. Carries about one layer per trip.

nodes.title: BuilDrone 2
nodes.summary: Second builder. Prints while BuilDrone 1 refills, so layers stay continuous.

nodes.title: ScanDrone
nodes.summary: Camera drone that maps each new layer for the deviation check.

nodes.title: Fabrication method: aerial AM
nodes.summary: Aerial AM chosen over gantry and ground robots because the terrace is at height with no crane access.

nodes.title: Material: cement mix No.1
nodes.summary: Mix No.1 holds its shape best under downwash. Chosen after mix No.4 slumped in tests.

nodes.title: Toolpath: rounded Peano
nodes.summary: Shortest path per layer, so each layer fits one cartridge.

nodes.title: Release next layer
nodes.summary: Go, hold or adjust. Needs the latest scan, cure state, stability check, wind reading, material and battery.

nodes.title: Tolerance: 5 mm per layer
nodes.summary: Maximum deviation of the nozzle path from the design, reachable with the delta arm.

nodes.title: Payload: 202 mL per load
nodes.summary: Usable cartridge volume. About one layer per trip, so a refill after every layer.

nodes.title: Wind limit: 6 m/s for printing
nodes.summary: Set during the dry run. Above it, path tracking drifts and the extrusion is disturbed. Example value.

nodes.title: Mix open time
nodes.summary: The mix must be deposited before it starts to set in the cartridge.

nodes.title: Rooftop wind and temperature
nodes.summary: Anemometer and temperature on the terrace, polled every few minutes during the build.

nodes.title: Layer scan feed
nodes.summary: Mesh of each new layer from the ScanDrone, compared against the digital twin.

nodes.title: Drone telemetry
nodes.summary: Battery, motor and position health for every drone.

nodes.title: Dry run: light-trace flight
nodes.summary: Drones fly the full path with lights and no material, to check tracking and spacing.

nodes.title: Build day 2: layers 19–40
nodes.summary: Second print day. Crew: Lee (site lead), refill technician, Ecem on the layer gate.

nodes.title: Final laser scan
nodes.summary: Full scan of the as-built shell against the design, for acceptance.

nodes.title: Flight approval for rooftop operations
nodes.summary: Approval to fly several drones over the terrace. Needed before the dry run.

nodes.title: Refill and battery crew for build day 2
nodes.summary: One technician to refill cartridges and swap batteries every layer.

nodes.title: Mix test report
nodes.summary: Slump, flow and set-time results for mixes No.1 and No.4 under propeller downwash.

nodes.title: Zhang et al., Nature 2022
nodes.summary: Aerial additive manufacturing with multiple autonomous robots. Source for the process and limits.

scenario.title: Client brief
scenario.author: Jordan
scenario.text: Client email: we want a sculptural shell over the rooftop terrace, about 2.4 m high, enclosure only. The building has no crane access to the roof and the terrace is too small for a printer frame.
scenario.story: The brief already contains the reason drones make sense: height and no access.

scenario.title: Method chosen: aerial AM
scenario.author: Ecem
scenario.text: Method comparison: a gantry would not fit the terrace and a crane cannot reach it. Aerial AM is justified by access and height. Trade-offs accepted: slower printing, lighter material, many refill trips.
scenario.story: The first design decision is whether a drone is needed at all.
scenario.reason: Only method that reaches the site

scenario.title: Mix No.4 slumps under downwash
scenario.author: Ecem
scenario.text: Mix test report: mix No.4 flows best but slumps when the propeller downwash passes over a fresh layer. Mix No.1 holds its shape. Switching the design to mix No.1; open time gets shorter.
scenario.story: Material tests change a design decision before anything is printed.
scenario.reason: Slump measured on three test layers

scenario.title: Dry run passes; wind limit set
scenario.author: Lee
scenario.text: Dry run with lights, no material: both builders tracked the path within tolerance and kept safe spacing at the narrowest layer. Tracking drifted above 6 m/s gusts, so the wind limit for printing is 6 m/s.
scenario.story: The safety gate before printing sets a limit that every later layer is checked against.
scenario.reason: Tracking logs from the dry run

scenario.title: Layers 16–18 drift outward
scenario.author: Lee
scenario.text: Layer scans 16, 17 and 18 each show the wall 6–7 mm outside the design on the north side. Path offsets have not corrected it.
scenario.story: Small drift is absorbed by offsets. Three layers in a row means the design has to change.
scenario.reason: Revise layers 19 and up in the twin; stability re-checked

scenario.title: Gusts above the limit
scenario.author: Lee
scenario.text: Rooftop anemometer: gusts of 8 m/s for the last 10 minutes, above the 6 m/s printing limit. Layer 23 is loaded and waiting.
scenario.story: The layer gate holds a loaded layer while the material's open time runs down.
scenario.reason: Hold; refill with fresh mix if the wait passes the open time

scenario.title: BuilDrone 2 battery fault
scenario.author: Lee
scenario.text: bd2 battery cell fault, grounded for the day
scenario.story: A short field message. The system ties it to the builder scheduled for the next layers.
scenario.reason: Continue with BuilDrone 1 alone, refilling between layers; slower but continuous

scenario.title: Final scan: within tolerance
scenario.author: Ecem
scenario.text: Final laser scan of the shell against the design: median deviation within tolerance, local exceedance on the north side at layers 16–18, absorbed by the redesign of the upper layers.
scenario.story: Acceptance with notes, every decision traceable to its evidence.
